messages.subject: error in CFA
parts:
Dear all
 
I'm relatively new in lavaan and R and I tried to fit the model below (based on het CHC-model of intelligence with a 3-level structure), but I'm getting the following error:
Error in if (lavpartable$free[var.f.idx] == 0 && lavpartable$ustart[var.f.idx] == : missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed
The model is based on 11 observed variables (N=1500). You can find my script below. Please tell me if you need more information.
 
CHC.model <- ' 
#latent variables
Gf =~ 1*PuntRJ + FigRJ
Gc =~ 1*SchiftJ + TegJ
Gsm =~ 1*GaTOT + GehBJ
Gv =~ 1*GeFigTot + DoPlJ
Gs =~ 1*GeCoA1 + GeCoA2 + GeCoA3 
Gtot =~ 1*Gf + Gc + Gsm + Gv + Gs 
#residual variances
PuntRJ ~~ PuntRJ; FigRJ ~~ FigRJ; SchiftJ ~~ SchiftJ; TegJ ~~ TegJ;
GaTOT ~~ GaTOT; GehBJ ~~ GehBJ; GeFigTot ~~ GeFigTot; DoPlJ ~~ DoPlJ;
GeCoA1 ~~ GeCoA1; GeCoA2 ~~ GeCoA2; GeCoA3 ~~ GeCoA3
 ' 
 fit<- lavaan(model = CHC.model, data = ITCCFA)
Error in if (lavpartable$free[var.f.idx] == 0 && lavpartable$ustart[var.f.idx] == : missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed
 
Thank you for your reply
Kind regards
Marlies

messages.subject: RE: error in CFA
parts:
Marlies—

     This syntax needs to say something more about the factors.  Currently, it does not say anything about the variances / residual variances of the factors.  If you used the sem function in the lavaan package instead of the lavaan function, I believe defaults would take care of this issue.  Try changing the function to sem, instead.

--Ed Rigdon

On 06/12/2014 05:34 PM, Edward Rigdon wrote:
> Marlies—
>
> This syntax needs to say something more about the factors.
> Currently, it does not say anything about the variances / residual
> variances of the factors. If you used the sem function in the lavaan
> package instead of the lavaan function, I believe defaults would take
> care of this issue. Try changing the function to sem, instead.

If you are new, please use the sem() function. The lavaan() functions is
very unforgiving when you 'forget' to specify some essential parameters:
for all variables, observed or latent, you need to specify a variance.

If you must use the lavaan() function, you can use the auto.var=TRUE
argument. This argument adds all needed variances if they are not
specified in the model syntax.

Yves.
